subject: Private observability: what Redwood will call “supported” (minimum pack scope + timeline)
related_links: Confluence (draft): Private observability minimum signals standard
body:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@heliohealth.com>, Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Private observability: what Redwood will call “supported” (minimum pack scope + timeline)

Ava/Daniel — following up from yesterday’s technical deep dive. Below is the crisp definition of what Redwood will call “supported observability” for Redwood Private, plus timeline + scope boundaries.

What “supported” means (Redwood Private – Observability Minimum Pack)
If you deploy the minimum pack as shipped (or equivalent config), Redwood Support/Solutions will treat the environment as having a supported baseline for troubleshooting. Concretely:

1) Metrics: Prometheus-compatible scrape endpoints and metric names/labels aligned with our minimum signals standard.
   - Must cover gateway/API, runtime (prefill/decode), GPU utilization, saturation/queueing, routing/fallback, control plane health, installer/upgrade health.
   - Cardinality guardrails: route/model/tenant labels must exist, but we provide defaults to avoid unbounded values.

2) Dashboards: Grafana dashboards provisioned from our bundle (or imported without modification).
   - You can customize, but “supported” assumes our baseline dashboards remain available for triage.

3) Alerts: PrometheusRule set installed (or rules functionally equivalent), with default severity mapping.
   - We’re biasing toward SLO burn-rate alerts + pipeline health checks to keep noise low.

4) Logs: structured logs shipped from gateway/runtime/control plane via a supported collector configuration.
   - Supported default: Vector or Fluent Bit (pack includes one recommended config + filters/sampling knobs).
   - Forwarding targets: customer SIEM/log backend, or object storage (depending on your standard tooling).

What “supported” does NOT mean
- Redwood does not require (or operate) a new observability backend in your environment.
- We won’t block go-live if you have an existing stack, but if the minimum required signals are missing, troubleshooting becomes “best effort” until the baseline is met.
- Bespoke dashboards/alerts outside the baseline are out of scope for the minimum pack.

Timeline (current plan)
- Beta bundle available for Private installs: early Feb 2025 (target)
- GA bundle integrated into the Private installer: March 2025 (target)

If helpful, I can share a 1-page PDF we’ve been using internally that summarizes the above.

Best,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Product (Private), Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 10:41 AM PST
Subject: Re: Private observability: what Redwood will call “supported” (minimum pack scope + timeline)

Ava — jumping in with the “what we see in real installs” view.

On (1): today, most Private customers already have Prometheus/Grafana standards. The minimum pack is designed to work in either mode:
- Option A (common): customer-managed Prometheus + Grafana; Redwood provides dashboards/rules + provisioning manifests.
- Option B (supported for fast starts): we can deploy a minimal in-cluster Grafana + Prometheus in the private environment, but you still own the retention/storage sizing decisions.

On (2): audit logging depends on your Grafana deployment mode.
- If you use your existing Grafana integrated to your IdP, you typically already have audit controls (plus we recommend configuration to log dashboard/rule changes).
- If we deploy Grafana in-cluster, we provide secure defaults (no anonymous access; RBAC baseline), and we document what to enable for audit trails.

Naomi may want to add specifics on audit logging expectations.

Markus
Solutions / Pro Services (Private)
Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 11:18 AM PST
Subject: Re: Private observability: what Redwood will call “supported” (minimum pack scope + timeline)

Adding a bit more color on audit logging.

Minimum pack includes:
- Guidance + recommended configuration to ensure access to Grafana and changes to dashboards/rules are attributable (RBAC + non-anonymous access + log retention guidance).
- Integration points for exporting audit-relevant logs from the observability components to your SIEM (where your org requires it).

Boundaries:
- The pack does not replace your enterprise audit program; it gives a “secure by default” baseline and clear knobs to meet common regulated requirements.
- Exact evidence artifacts (e.g., screenshots/log excerpts) are typically produced during your deployment validation / go-live checklist.

If you share your audit control list (even a subset), we can map the minimum pack defaults and highlight any gaps.

Naomi
Security & Compliance Product Lead
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 12:07 PM PST
Subject: Re: Private observability: what Redwood will call “supported” (minimum pack scope + timeline)

Ava — on the “supported” requirement itself, we’re intentionally defining it in terms of signals + dashboards/alerts being present and working, not in terms of a single mandated vendor deployment.

The only “hard line” is: we need a Prometheus-compatible path for rules/queries (because our bundled rules and dashboards assume that). If you’re using a different TSDB behind the scenes, that’s fine as long as PromQL compatibility is real and the required metrics/labels exist.

Re: audit logging: looping in Sean as well since he’s leading paging/alerting policy. From an ops perspective, we also care about having a clear owner for:
- who can change alert rules
- how changes get reviewed
- how paging destinations are configured

Separate note: we’ve seen a failure mode where rules don’t load after an upgrade (promtool parse issues). The GA pack includes validation checks post-install to catch this early.

I’m attaching the 1-pager we referenced.

Attachment: Redwood-Private-Observability-Min-Pack-Supported-Definition-v0.4.pdf

Vivek

Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 12:32 PM PST
Subject: Re: Private observability: what Redwood will call “supported” (minimum pack scope + timeline)

Ava/Daniel — confirming the alerting posture:

- Baseline alerts: primarily SLO burn-rate + a small set of “hard down” alerts (availability, rule loading failures, pipeline health, resource exhaustion).
- Default thresholds are conservative; they’re intended to be safe for most environments and not page on normal load variation.
- We provide a tuning workflow (what to adjust first, what we do NOT recommend) and a standard way to suppress known maintenance windows.

Operationally, the “supported” bar is that alerts can be evaluated and will fire when the underlying condition exists (i.e., rule loading is healthy + metrics present). We don’t require you to page Redwood; we require that the system is diagnosable.

Sean
SRE Lead (Observability/SLOs)
Redwood Inference

From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@heliohealth.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@heliohealth.com>

Date: Thu, Jan 16, 2025 at 4:38 PM PST
Subject: Re: Private observability: what Redwood will call “supported” (minimum pack scope + timeline)

Daniel — migrating from in-cluster to centralized Prometheus/Grafana is a supported path.

The pack is versioned and portable: dashboards/rules are shipped as a bundle and can be provisioned into either Grafana instance. The only thing you’ll typically need to re-point is:
- data source configuration
- alert receiver routing (PagerDuty/Opsgenie/Slack/webhooks)
- log forwarding target (SIEM endpoint / TLS settings)

We’re putting the migration steps in the operator docs, but in the meantime, attached is a short internal FAQ with the “supported” definition and common questions.

Attachment: Private-Observability-Min-Pack-FAQ-v0.2.docx

If you want, share what your centralized stack is (Prometheus/Mimir/Thanos, Grafana Cloud, etc.) and we’ll confirm compatibility assumptions.

Elliot Price
Docs Lead (Operator Documentation)
Redwood Inference
